summary: The single finding (low) is confirmed, but on corrected grounds and with a corrected fix. Item 31's trace-formula half is indeed planned by none of its cited stages: EDC.8 says 'Ordinary Frobenius point counting is still PR196 TraceFormula's theorem'. But the item never cited R34.1 for the trace formula. Its note assigns R34.1 to 'the Frobenius/weight conventions' and the trace formula to EDC.8 through YZ17 Proposition A.12. R34.1 never planned a trace formula, before or after RS-17, and RS-17 keeps exactly the Frobenius normalization the note cites it for. So the defect has been present since the extraction, and it sits in the EDC.8 citation, not in RS-17. The planned list cannot hold PR196, because check_paper.py accepts only atlas layers. The atlas convention, followed by four accepted extractions, is SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2, the integration owner of the CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers, with PR196 named in the note. The authorised change is item 31's planned list and note, plus two sentences of PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24.md. The paper review is not edited. Disclosure: this verifier red-teamed PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17 (PR #4961), which compared this extraction's Part II grouping and Octahedron Lemma note, and whose finding /8(a) gave the same scheme-level owner, PR196, for YZ17's own use of the trace formula.

sources.citation: Feng, Yun and Zhang, Higher Siegel–Weil formula for unitary groups: the non-singular terms, arXiv 2103.11514v4 (29 November 2023), 79 pp. The hash equals the one the extraction recorded for v4, and the extraction records that v4 and the published version carry the same 112 numbered statements. Read the introduction's outline (§1.4), §5.1–5.2 (Definition 5.2, Theorem 5.3 and its proof, pp. 34–35), the proof of Proposition 5.6 with (5.10) (pp. 35–36), and §11.2–11.3 (Definition 11.6, Propositions 11.7–11.8 and their proofs, Corollaries 11.9–11.10, pp. 70–73), plus the use of the function-sheaf dictionary in §12 (Theorems 12.1–12.2, p. 74).

Invent. Math. 235 (2024) 569–668, the version of record the extraction read. Not read: link.springer.com returned an HTML bot-check page instead of the PDF to a non-browser client. The finding concerns item 31's owners, not a quoted statement, so the preprint is enough. The statement numbers used here match the extraction's locators (Theorem 5.3, Propositions 11.7–11.8).

findings.reason: Checked at 8044fa30. None of the files involved has changed since the red team's input 113e7bcb or up to origin/main 5a2aecc2: the extraction and its .md, REV-PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24, data/atlas.json, data/restructure/RS-17.result.json, the EDC and WeightsInEtaleCohomology READMEs, and PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/19. No Lean declaration is involved. The pinned baseline's declarations.tsv has no Lefschetz or TraceFormula declaration, so 'PR 196' is an upstream roadmap contract (TauCetiRoadmap CohomologicalPointCounting/TraceFormula), not library code. (a) What holds. Item 31 ('Cohomological correspondences, the Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula and the sheaf-to-function dictionary', planned [EDC.8, R34.1]) bundles two inputs. The paper uses both. The Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula is invoked by name in the proof of Theorem 5.3 ('By the Grothendieck-Lefschetz trace formula, we have Tr(Fr, K^Eis_d(T)_Q) = Σ_i Σ_{(I,Q)∈Herm_{i,2d}(k)} …') and again after (5.10) in the proof of Proposition 5.6. The function-sheaf dictionary is §12's matching ('sheaves on A_d which correspond to the two sides of (12.2), in the sense of the function-sheaf dictionary'). EDC.8 plans correspondences, composition and the trace class, but excludes the numerical formula: 'Ordinary Frobenius point counting is still PR196 TraceFormula's theorem … An arbitrary fixed-point set does not supply a numerical trace.' EDC.8 had the same text at the extraction's commit c6116e19. R34.1 ('Frobenius, algebraicity and weights') plans no trace formula. So the trace-formula half of item 31 is planned by neither cited stage. The same conclusion was reached for the parallel item PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19/120, which REV-PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-19 moved from planned [EDC.8] to missing because EDC.8 'leaves Frobenius point counting to the trace-formula roadmap'. Low is right: the theorem already has an owner (PR196), so nothing new is built and only the citation changes. (b) Corrections to the red team. First, item 31 does not cite R34.1 for the trace formula. Its note reads 'EDC.8 plans cohomological correspondences and their trace classes; R34.1 the Frobenius/weight conventions. Proposition 11.8 rests on the Lefschetz trace formula of [YZ17, Proposition A.12] (routed to EDC.8 by PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17).' The misattribution is to EDC.8. Second, RS-17 is not the cause. At c6116e19 (2026-09-22 18:56 UTC, before REV-RS-17 at 2026-09-23 13:13 UTC), R34.1 already read 'Import DWP.0's Weil numbers … Prove the representation-convention adapter on the imported Frobenius action', with no trace formula. RS-17's narrowed R34.1 still keeps 'Arithmetic/geometric Frobenius, dual/Tate/embedding normalization', which is the role the note gives it. The citation of R34.1 is therefore still correct. The defect dates from the extraction, and the review missed it. The review's line 'EDC.8 and R34.1 for correspondences and traces' is loose, but it is a record of that review and is not edited. Third, 'WC.0 and WC.1 import from it' is half right: WC.1 requires UPSTREAM:CohomologicalPointCounting:TraceFormula, but WC.0 requires EllAdicRealization and FrobeniusGeometry. Fourth, the fix's main form ('Name … CohomologicalPointCounting/TraceFormula (PR 196)' as planner) would fail scripts/check_paper.py, which rejects any planned entry that 'is not a layer of the atlas'. PR196 has no atlas stage. The atlas records SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 as the integration owner of the UPSTREAM:CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers ('Integrate CohomologicalPointCounting suppliers'). The accepted extractions PAPER-DELIGNE-74 (1.12.1), PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16/45, PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24 and PAPER-LIU-WOOD-ZUREICKBROWN-24/44 all mark the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula planned at SF.2, and name PR196 in the note. Fifth, the red team did not use the confirmed RT-AREA-etale/3: EDC is scheme-only, and Herm_{2d}(X′/X) and Lagr_{2d} are algebraic stacks. The paper itself reduces the stack case to schemes by a smooth scheme cover in the proof of Proposition 11.8 (item 27), and Theorem 5.3 uses the formula stalkwise at Q ∈ Herm_{2d}(k). General sheaf theory on stacks is RT-AREA-etale/3's proposed stacks Part II (ST.1–ST.6), whose edit 9 to this extraction's route 1 brief is pending a verdict. Authorised fix scope. Severity is low, so no FIX-RT job is generated. If the files are next edited for another reason, make these changes. (1) In research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24.result.json, item PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24/31 only: add SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 to planned, keeping EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.8 and WeightsInEtaleCohomology:R34.1. Rewrite the note to say four things. EDC.8 plans cohomological correspondences, their composition and trace classes. The Grothendieck–Lefschetz trace formula with sheaf coefficients and the trace function of a complex, on schemes, are the upstream PR196 CohomologicalPointCounting TraceFormula theorem (EDC.8: 'Ordinary Frobenius point counting is still PR196 TraceFormula's theorem'), integrated at SF.2 as in PAPER-DELIGNE-74, PAPER-SCHMIDT-STIX-16 and PAPER-BERGSTROM-FABER-PAYNE-24. R34.1 supplies the arithmetic/geometric Frobenius normalization, which it keeps after RS-17. The Frobenius-graph formula [YZ17, Proposition A.12] behind Proposition 11.8 is PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17/35, which is missing and source-routed by that extraction, and its generalization with the stack reduction is this extraction's item 27, in the Part II. Keep the id, name, statement, locator and status planned. Re-run check_paper.py. (2) In PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24.md, add SF.2 (the PR196 trace formula) to the 'Planned' bullet. Correct the Validation sentence 'none is restructured or retired' to say that RS-17 narrowed R34.1 to Frobenius normalization adapters, which is the use cited. Not authorised: editing REV-PAPER-FENG-YUN-ZHANG-24.md, removing R34.1, splitting item 31 into two items (optional and not needed, since one planned list covers both halves), changing status to missing, and any edit to route 1 or to the other extractions. The stack extension belongs to RT-AREA-etale's fix and its pending verdicts. Disclosure: this verifier red-teamed PAPER-YUN-ZHANG-17 (PR #4961). Its finding /2 concerns the shared GlobalShtukas Part II grouping, its finding /3 corrects this extraction's item 32 note on the Octahedron Lemma, and its finding /8(a) named PR196 for schemes, with the stack case at ST.6 or YZ19/227, as the owner of the Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula in YZ17. This verdict does not judge those findings or items 26, 27 and 32.
